original_query: select e.mgr, d.mgr from emp as e full outer join emp as d on e.mgr = d.mgr group by d.mgr, e.mgr

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Eliminate the redundant self FULL OUTER JOIN: since both aliases (e and d) reference the same unfiltered emp table, every non-null mgr value on one side always has a matching value on the other side. No unmatched non-null rows can exist, so the join is entirely redundant.
Replace the two-column GROUP BY (d.mgr, e.mgr) over the massive join output with a single-column GROUP BY mgr directly on emp, projecting mgr twice to preserve the original two-column output schema.

The previous report's equivalence concern is incorrect: NULL mgr rows do not match in the full outer join, but they are emitted as unmatched rows and then collapsed by GROUP BY into a single (NULL, NULL) row. GROUP BY mgr preserves exactly the same NULL behavior (one NULL group if any NULL exists).
